groups.title: Sohra Culture & Experience Centre
groups.body: A cultural destination organised around water, performance and a public street. Roof forms draw on the Khasi knup, bringing local references into a contemporary ensemble of galleries, gathering spaces and hospitality.

groups.title: Umiam Lake
groups.body: A collection of lakefront, cultural, residential and landscape studies around Umiam Lake. The work spans the public waterfront redevelopment and a wider masterplan for music, film, wellness, accommodation, craft and adventure.

slides.title: The wider lake masterplan
slides.body: Development clusters follow the terrain and retain the lake as the principal organising element.

slides.title: The public waterfront
slides.body: The detailed lakefront plan arranges arrival, recreation, food and cultural programmes as a walkable sequence.

slides.title: A family of lakefront buildings

slides.title: The market

slides.body: The drawing studies test the relationship between structure, enclosure and the open public edge.

slides.title: Arrival & construction detail
slides.body: The arrival structures carry the architectural language into the boundary and entrance sequence.

slides.body: Performance spaces, rehearsal and production facilities form a shared campus for learning, making and public gathering.

slides.body: The wider vision includes therapy, rehabilitation, meditation and accommodation. These are programme and masterplan studies within the lake development.

slides.title: Film City & Lakeside Hotel

slides.body: The wider programme also explores an Adventure Park, Echo Island, a Craft Village, glamping, the MECL Circuit House and a Sailing Club. Music-related components include a performing arts centre, recording studios, an ethno-musical centre and artist residencies. These are components of the Umiam masterplan vision, with different levels of design development.

groups.title: What Bodoland Needs
groups.body: A regional design study that links cultural identity and landscape to possible civic, tourism and infrastructure interventions. The framework recognises distinct roles for different districts rather than treating the region as a single development site.

Kokrajhar: administration and culture
Chirang: ecology and agriculture
Baksa: adventure and resilience
Tamulpur: new civic development
